title: The city x category event hubs had no inbound links: only the sitemap reached /discover/events/in/<city>/<category>

source.ref: found 2026-10-05 by the scan-seven SEO/GEO finders (26-agent fan-out), confirmed by hand against the tree

detail: FOUND 2026-10-05 (scan seven, seo-local finder). A search of app/, components/ and lib/ for events/in/ found one link: the hub page's own sibling row. The city landing pages (/discover/cities/<city> and /discover/places/<city>) linked only the generic /discover/events, so the pages that match a local query most closely ('Movement in Encinitas') were orphaned from the crawl. CLOSED 2026-10-05: both city pages read getCityCategoryHubs (fail-safe to none) and draw an 'Events by type in <city>' pill row with the hub page's own markup under the events list.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const miss=["app/discover/cities/[citySlug]/page.tsx","app/discover/places/[citySlug]/page.tsx"].filter((p)=>!/\/discover\/events\/in\/\$\{h\.citySlug\}\/\$\{h\.category\.slug\}/.test(fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8")));if(miss.length){console.error("SCAN-670: "+miss.join(", ")+" link(s) no city x category event hub, so /discover/events/in/<city>/<category>, the pages that match a local query most closely, are reachable from the sitemap alone.");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Fails on main before this change; passes with it.
